g.text: D Splits on activation, not lineage
Cluster 6 (781 cells; provisional 'Trm-like CD8') carries a shared Trm/IEL program but contains both CD8 and CD4 T cells. (A) Among 586 cells with a detectable lineage
marker, 66% are CD8 and 34% CD4; a further 187 (24%) had no detectable Cd4/Cd8a/Cd8b1 (dropout) and 8 were double-positive, both left unassigned (majority-vote imputation of
the dropout cells gives a concordant 61/39, robustness check only). (B) CD8 and CD4 module scores form two arms. (C) The cluster expresses both lineages' markers on a shared
Trm/IEL program vs clean CD8 (Teff CD8-like) and CD4 (Th2-like) references. (D-E) Lineage is NOT a separable axis: unsupervised sub-clustering (max silhouette 0.13 at res
0.2) splits on immediate-early/stress genes (Atf3, Fosb, Dusp1, Nr4a1, Fos; sub-cluster 1) not on Cd4/Cd8 — the activation module score segregates by sub-cluster while the
Trm score is uniform and Cd8a/Cd4 scatter across both, and every sub-cluster stays CD4/CD8-mixed. Doublets were ruled out (scDblFinder 1.2%, lowest of any T-cell cluster;
Tcell_doublet_check.R). The dominant transcriptional axis is a shared Trm/IEL + activation program; CD4/CD8 lineage is a minor axis the data does not resolve. The cluster is
annotated 'Trm type mixed CD8+ CD4' rather than split, and excluded from CD4/CD8-specific analyses.
Supplementary — justification of the 'Trm type mixed CD8+ CD4' annotation (cluster 6)
